summary: Place board orchestration in its own application slice. The board RSC read composes independently owned work-item and label capabilities, then applies board-only policy before returning serializable view data. Work-items and labels never import one another.

tree.purpose: Board DTOs, status-group types, label-view types, and transport-neutral error types.
Valibot schemas for board query/input and returned data boundaries.
Board-owned ports for authorized work-item and label reads; depends only on domain contracts.
Orchestrates both reads and applies hide-archived, status grouping, visible-label attachment, and unauthorized-label rejection.
Implements the board work-item port by calling the work-items capability’s trusted server read API.
Implements the board label port by calling the labels capability’s trusted server read API.
Server-only composition root that creates board ports, auth context, logging, and cache dependencies.
`server-only` authenticated read entrypoint; verifies the actor, invokes the composed use-case, and returns DTOs.
Thin RSC route entrypoint that reads URL filters, calls the board DAL, and renders the board view.
Presentation-only board rendering by status groups, including visible label details and safe warnings.
Use-case tests with fake work-item and label ports.
Contract/mapping/error tests for each capability adapter.
Auth and DTO-boundary tests for the server-only read entrypoint.
Rendering tests for groups, archived-item exclusion, and partial label references.
Authenticated end-to-end board flow against real persistence and authorization.

flows: RSC flow: `src/app/board/page.tsx` → `src/dal/board/get-board.ts` → `src/infrastructure/board/composition.ts` → `src/use-cases/board/get-board.ts` → work-item and label ports → their independent outbound adapters → trusted capability server APIs → persistence.

Policy flow: fetch actor-visible work items and label details → remove archived items → reject/omit label references not returned as actor-visible → attach remaining label DTOs → group items by status → return serializable board DTO.

Authorization flow: DAL derives the current actor from the server session and rejects unauthenticated requests; the actor context is passed to both capability APIs, which independently re-check authorization.

Failure flow: authentication failure becomes redirect/unauthorized; work-item or label backend failure fails the board read with a safe page error and captured server telemetry; an individual unauthorized or missing label is omitted fail-closed and recorded as a non-sensitive board warning.

Cache flow: the RSC/DAL owns the read cache. Tags are scoped to the actor/tenant and board-relevant work-item and label data; mutations in either capability invalidate their own scoped tags. The board does not own either persistence cache.

decisions.rationale: Grouping, archived filtering, label attachment, and label rejection are board behavior, not work-item or label persistence behavior.

decisions.choice: Board use-case depends on ports; adapters implement those ports.
decisions.rationale: The use-case remains framework- and persistence-independent, while work-items and labels remain independently changeable.

decisions.choice: Expose narrow trusted server read contracts from work-items and labels; consume them through board adapters.
decisions.rationale: The board needs stable capability contracts without importing private repositories or coupling the two capabilities together.

decisions.choice: RSC page → server-only DAL; no Route Handler or TanStack Query.
decisions.rationale: This is a read-heavy first-party page without polling, infinite scrolling, or browser-owned cache lifecycle.

decisions.choice: Defense in depth at DAL and both capability APIs.
decisions.rationale: `proxy.ts` may protect navigation but cannot be the data authorization boundary; label visibility must be enforced server-side.

decisions.choice: Fail closed by omitting inaccessible label details and emitting a safe warning.
decisions.rationale: The board must never expose labels the actor cannot view, while one stale or invalid label reference need not hide the entire work item.

decisions.choice: Use-cases return/throw transport-neutral application errors; DAL maps them to safe UI errors and telemetry.
decisions.rationale: No database/provider messages or sensitive authorization details should reach the client.

decisions.choice: Test policy with fake ports, adapters against their lowest transport boundary, and one real authenticated E2E flow.
decisions.rationale: This verifies both architectural seams and the actual authorization/data composition.

risks: The board’s cache key/tag must include tenant and actor scope to prevent cross-user data leakage.
Capability API contracts should distinguish unauthorized, not-found, and dependency failure so the board can omit only safe individual label references.
If board filters or pagination are added later, keep them in the board use-case and validate URL-derived inputs at the DAL boundary.
